messages.content:
" *

Creates a random string whose length is the number of characters * specified.

* *

Characters will be chosen from the set of characters specified.

* * @param count the length of random string to create * @param chars the character array containing the set of characters to use, * may be null * @return the random string * @throws IllegalArgumentException if {@code count} < 0. "

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the failing test expects:
  - RandomStringUtilsTest.testExceptions() asserts that invalid inputs throw IllegalArgumentException (IAE), including the case RandomStringUtils.random(1, new char[0]) (an empty character array).

- Call flow for the failing case:
  1) test invokes RandomStringUtils.random(1, new char[0]).
     - random(int, char...) at lines 317–322:
       - Since chars != null (it’s an empty array), it delegates to:
         random(count, 0, chars.length, false, false, chars, RANDOM)
       - With an empty array, chars.length == 0, so start = 0, end = 0.
  2) Inside random(int, int, int, boolean, boolean, char[], Random) at lines 223–281:
     - Count is positive, so no early return or IAE (lines 225–229).
     - Because start == 0 and end == 0:
       - And both letters == false and numbers == false,
       - end is set to Integer.MAX_VALUE (lines 231–237).
     - gap = end - start becomes a very large number (line 241).
     - In the while loop, since chars != null (even though empty), it executes:
       ch = chars[random.nextInt(gap) + start]; (line 248)

- Why this fails:
  - chars is an empty array, so any access chars[...], regardless of index, throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
  - The method decides to use chars[] solely based on chars != null (line 245), without checking for chars.length == 0.
  - Additionally, when start == 0 and end == 0 with letters == false and numbers == false, it expands the numeric range (end = Integer.MAX_VALUE), which is unrelated to the provided chars[] and guarantees an invalid index into the empty array.

- Relation to the bug report:
  - The report notes that random(count, 0, 0, false, false, universe, random) throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when the array is empty or end is 0. This matches the observed behavior: once start and end are both 0 and chars != null, the code still indexes into chars[] with an index derived from a large gap, causing AIOOBE.
  - The test expects an IllegalArgumentException for an empty provided char array, but the current implementation does not validate empty arrays and instead fails with AIOOBE.

- Summary of root cause:
  - Missing validation for empty chars[] in RandomStringUtils.random overloads that accept a char array.
  - In the core method, choosing the chars[] branch based on chars != null without handling the empty-array case, combined with the start/end reset logic when both are zero, leads to invalid indexing and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of the expected IllegalArgumentException.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
